Onboarding Guide · v1.0

Run liquidation the governed way.

LCC is the control panel your team uses to decide how excess and end-of-life inventory is moved, thresholded, and approved — with every change reviewed before it goes live and permanently recorded.

⏱️ ~15 min read 👥 For planning, ops & approvers 🧭 5 modules, 1 workflow 🔒 No change is silent
01 · Why LCC exists

1 Goals & what you can do

Liquidation used to live in scattered spreadsheets and one-off requests. LCC replaces that with a single, governed place to configure the liquidation engine and sign off on what it produces.

🎯

One control panel

Routing, thresholds, product rules and approvals in one place — no more spreadsheet drift.

🛡️

Safe by default

Nothing changes until you explicitly Commit. Mistakes stay in draft, never in production.

🧾

Fully auditable

Every committed change is stamped with who, what, when, and a before → after diff.

Who uses it

  • Planners / Ops — configure warehouses, thresholds and product rules.
  • Approvers — review the engine's proposed batch and authorize or reject it.
  • Auditors / Leadership — trace exactly what changed and why.

Key terms (worth 60 seconds)

Master Sink
The destination warehouse that all liquidated inventory routes to by default.
Donor
A warehouse that contributes stock to liquidation. Donors can be bypassed to hide them from the engine.
Route Pair Override
An exception that sends one specific donor's stock to a different sink instead of the Master Sink.
Transfer Threshold (Minimum Viable Load)
The financial circuit-breaker — the min/max COGS, units and weight a transfer must satisfy to be allowed.
Precedence
When rules overlap, the most specific wins: SKU → Brand → Global.
Shelf-life % & OP
The point in a product's life where it becomes liquidation-eligible. OP = Outdated Packaging stock.
Batch
A set of transfer orders the engine generates for you to review and approve.
Draft → Commit
The two-step model behind every change: stage it, review it, then commit it live.

03 · The one workflow to learn

3 How every change works: Draft → Commit

This is the single most important concept in LCC. You cannot break production by editing. Every edit — a toggle, a number, an override — is staged as a pending change. It only affects the live liquidation engine when you commit.

✏️

1. Stage

Make edits anywhere. Each shows a Pending badge and increments the sidebar counter.

👀

2. Review

Click Draft Mode to see everything staged, or open the Audit → Pending tab for full detail.

🚀

3. Commit

Commit Configuration applies all changes at once and writes an audit entry. Or Discard to throw them away.

Rule of thumb: configure freely, commit deliberately. If in doubt, open Draft Mode and read the list before you commit — or hit Discard all changes to reset.
04 · Real scenarios

4 Use cases

The most common jobs teams do in LCC, each mapped to where you do it.

A. Point all liquidation to a new sink warehouse

Standing up a new liquidation hub? Search for it under Warehouse → Warehouse Network and set it as Master Sink. Every donor now routes there by default.

B. Temporarily take a warehouse out of liquidation

A site is doing a stock-take or is short-staffed. Warehouse → Donor Network, flip its toggle to Bypassed. The engine stops proposing transfers from it — no data is deleted.

C. Send one warehouse's stock to a different sink

Mumbai should ship to Kolkata instead of the default hub for a season. Warehouse → Route Pair Overrides → + Add override, pick donor → sink.

D. Raise the financial floor for transfers

Too many tiny, uneconomical transfers? Increase the minimum COGS/units/weight under Transfer Thresholds. Set a network-wide Global default, then add Category or Brand overrides where needed (remember precedence: Brand > Category > Global).

E. Tune what becomes liquidation-eligible

Control shelf-life triggers and which classes/brands/SKUs are in scope under Products. Disable a whole class, set a brand-level shelf-life %, or override a single SKU — precedence resolves conflicts automatically.

F. Review & authorize an engine batch

When the engine proposes a batch, an approver reviews the orders and line items, then types the Liquidation Identifier into the Authorization Gate to authorize (or rejects it).

G. Prove what changed, and when

For a review or a “who touched this?” question, open Audit Log. Filter by module, action or user; expand any row for the before → after diff; export to CSV.

05 · Guided how-tos

5 Step-by-step (the main paths)

Not exhaustive — these cover the routes you'll use most. Every path ends the same way: Commit.

Change the Master Sink

  1. Go to Warehouse → Warehouse Network.
  2. Type a warehouse name/ID/city in the search box.
  3. On the matching card, click Set as Master Sink.
  4. Confirm the header chip updates, then Commit Configuration.

Bypass or re-enable a donor

  1. Open Warehouse → Donor Network.
  2. Find the warehouse (search or the All/Enabled/Disabled filter).
  3. Flip the Participation toggle. A Pending badge appears.
  4. Commit to apply.

Add a route pair override

  1. Warehouse → Route Pair Overrides → + Add override.
  2. Pick the Donor, then the Sink from the searchable dropdowns.
  3. Click Add override (edit the destination later via the pencil icon; toggle off to remove).
  4. Commit.

Edit a threshold

  1. Open Transfer Thresholds and choose Global, Category, or Brand.
  2. Click any MIN/MAX value to edit it inline; press Enter to save (Esc cancels).
  3. For a new override, use + Add override and pick the category/brand.
  4. Commit.

Set a shelf-life / SKU rule

  1. Go to Products. Use Global Rules for network defaults and class on/off switches.
  2. Use Brand Overrides or SKU Configuration for specifics; click a % to edit, toggle eligibility as needed.
  3. Check the Source badge (SKU / Brand / Global) to see which rule wins.
  4. Commit.

Authorize a batch

  1. Open Transfer Approval → Pending Approval.
  2. Expand orders to inspect line items and expiry flags.
  3. Type the batch's Liquidation Identifier into the Authorization Gate — a green ✓ confirms a match.
  4. Click Authorize Batch (or Reject Batch). Manage in-flight orders under the Manage Transactions tab.
Bulk changes: Donor Network, Route Overrides, Brand and SKU screens each have a Bulk Upload via CSV panel — download the template, fill it, drop it back in. Uploaded rows are staged as pending changes just like manual edits.
06 · Questions

6 FAQ

If I change something, does it take effect immediately?
No. Edits are staged as pending changes and only go live when you click Commit Configuration. Until then the live engine is untouched.
I made a mistake while editing. How do I undo it?
If you haven't committed: click Discard all changes in the sidebar to drop everything staged, or just re-edit the value before committing. After committing, make a new corrective change — the Audit Log keeps the full history either way.
What does the amber “Pending” badge mean?
That item has an edit staged but not yet committed. The number next to Draft Mode in the sidebar is the total count of pending changes.
Two rules apply to the same product — which one wins?
The most specific one. Order of precedence is SKU override → Brand override → Global default. The Source badge on SKU rows tells you which is currently in effect.
What's the difference between “Bypassed” and deleting a warehouse?
Bypassing hides a donor from the liquidation engine but keeps all its data — it's reversible with one toggle. Nothing is deleted.
Why is the Master Sink's participation toggle disabled?
A Master Sink can't also be a donor to itself, so it's automatically protected from donor participation.
What is the Authorization Gate asking for?
The batch's Liquidation Identifier (e.g. LIQ-2024-0047), shown on the batch header. Typing the exact ID confirms you're authorizing the right batch before it's committed.
Can I make many changes at once?
Yes — two ways. Stage as many individual edits as you like and commit them together, or use the Bulk Upload via CSV panels on the relevant screens.
How do I show someone exactly what changed?
Open the Audit Log, filter by module/user/action, expand any row for the before → after diff, and use Export CSV to share it.
Something looks cramped on my screen.
Collapse the sidebar with the chevron for more width, and switch between light and dark mode from the bottom of the sidebar.
Is this the real system or a prototype?
This guide accompanies the interactive prototype. Data shown is representative sample data; the workflows, screens and controls mirror the intended production experience.
